messages.body_plain:
It is expected that you may have to tweak the converted vignette
manually. I hope Sweave2knitr() can quickly "fix" most of the obvious
problems, but it is certainly not intelligent enough to fix
everything.

On Mon, Feb 3, 2014 at 5:49 PM, Dan Tenenbaum <dand...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> Not sure if these are bugs or not but they were unexpected.
>
> I converted a Sweave vignette to knitr with Sweave2knitr().
>
> Afterwards I had to do the following things manually before knit2pdf() would
> succeed, and also before I could build the package.
>
> I had to comment out the following lines:
>
> \DefineVerbatimEnvironment{Sinput}{Verbatim}
> {formatcom = {\color{Sinput}}}
> \DefineVerbatimEnvironment{Soutput}{Verbatim}
> {formatcom = {\color{Soutput}}}
> \DefineVerbatimEnvironment{Scode}{Verbatim}
> {formatcom = {\color{Scode}}}
>

This is probably due to the fact that \usepackage{Sweave} is removed,
because Sweave.sty depends on fancyvrb, which contains the Verbatim
environment.

>
> I had to add library(knitr) to the first chunk, right before
> opts_chunk$set()
>
> This was not necessary for knit2pdf() to succeed, because obviously knitr is
> loaded before I call that. But it was necessary when running R CMD build on
> the package.

This makes sense. I just added library(knitr) before opts_chunk in the
development version.

>
> I had to change e.g.
>
> \centerline{\includegraphics[width=0.3\textwidth]{qpgraphSimulate-3regulargraph}}
>
>
> to
>
> \centerline{\includegraphics[width=0.3\textwidth]{figure/3regulargraph}}

I do not understand why this is necessary. I mean, why did you have to
write LaTeX code for figures? Doesn't this suffice?

<<3regulargraph, fig.align='center', out.width='.3\\textwidth'>>=
plot(1:10)
@

In the Sweave age, there was no way to specify the figure alignment or
output width, but knitr has solved the problem from day one.

>
>
>
>
> Not sure this was necessary, but I thought Sweave2knitr should have done it:
> adding to the beginning:
>
> %\VignetteEngine{knitr::knitr}

But not all .Rnw documents are package vignettes.

>
> And I also had to work around a bug mentioned in another thread
> (https://groups.google.com/d/msg/knitr/kUwmJPBoVvs/Ygv_GZwMqZYJ).
>
> Maybe I'm wrong, but it seems like Sweave2knitr() should be able to figure
> out most of these things.
>
> Thanks!
> Dan

Regards,
Yihui
--


This issue seems more related to operating system capability than application capability. You did not explicitly mention your OS, but from the error message I am guessing it is a Mac.
